title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, carried over from the previous page. There is an extension 1→π→E→G→1, with ρ ∈ G of order n. ρ also denotes a fixed lift in E with ρ^n = 1, and ρ(x) := ρxρ^{-1}.

Equation (8) is the condition on g ∈ π that ρ'_g = gρ again has order n. Equivalently, g·ρ(g)·…·ρ^{n-1}(g) = 1, the nonabelian 1-cocycle condition for Z/n acting on π via ρ.

The objects involved:
- Solutions g of (8) correspond to the lifts of order n of ρ.
- They also correspond to the splittings over Z/nZ of the restricted extension 1→π→π̃→Z/n→1.
- The π-ρ-conjugacy g ~ a g ρ(a)^{-1} (a ∈ π) is the twisted-conjugation equivalence.
- So the set of classes [g]_ρ is the nonabelian cohomology set H^1(Z/n, π), with distinguished point [1]_ρ.

On this page:
1. E_ρ := preimage in E of G^ρ = Centr_G(ρ) gives an extension (25): 1→π→E_ρ→G^ρ→1.
2. E_ρ acts on solutions of (8) by Θ(α): g ↦ α g ρ(α)^{-1}. This corresponds to conjugating the lift gρ by α. Because π ⊂ E_ρ is normal, the action descends to an action of G^ρ on H^1(Z/n, π).
3. For α ∈ E one has αρ(α)^{-1} = αρα^{-1}ρ^{-1} = [α,ρ]. This lies in π iff [ᾱ,ρ] = 1, i.e. iff α ∈ E_ρ.
4. A solution g may fail to be a π-coboundary aρ(a)^{-1} (a ∈ π) yet be an E_ρ-coboundary. This happens iff [g]_ρ lies in the G^ρ-orbit of the trivial class [1]_ρ.
5. The page then begins describing the set of α ∈ E_ρ with g = αρ(α)^{-1} (26). This is continued on the next page: it is a coset of the centralizer E^ρ, and becomes a torsor under it when π^ρ = 1.

In modern terms this is the standard nonabelian-cohomology statement (Serre, Cohomologie galoisienne I §5) for the sequence 1→π→E_ρ→G^ρ→1 with Z/n acting through ρ. The kernel of H^1(Z/n,π) → H^1(Z/n,E_ρ) is the orbit of the base point under H^0(Z/n, G^ρ) = G^ρ.

Purpose: classify conjugacy classes of torsion elements (finite cyclic subgroups) lifting a given ρ in an extension of profinite / fundamental groups. This serves the 'équation des lacets' programme following the Longue Marche: torsion in Teichmüller-type fundamental groups and the Galois/GT action.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. The computations αρ(α)^{-1} = [α,ρ] and the criterion α ∈ E_ρ are correct.
Notation is overloaded: ρ denotes both the element of G and its chosen lift in E. The page 'ρ(α)' means ρ α ρ^{-1} computed in E.
On the next page, 'ρ^n=1 i.e. ρ=1' is a slip for 'n=1'.

ideas.what: Lifts of order n of ρ ∈ G to E correspond to twisted cocycles g ∈ π. Conjugacy under π corresponds to twisted (ρ-)conjugacy, so the classes form H^1(Z/n, π).
ideas.modern_name: Nonabelian H^1 / conjugacy classes of complements (splittings) of an extension
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Schur–Zassenhaus context); nonabelian cohomology formalism by Serre, Grothendieck, Giraud (1950s–60s)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's Tohoku/torsor material and Giraud's nonabelian cohomology; the Longue Marche (1981) treats torsion in π_1 similarly

ideas.what: The centralizer preimage E_ρ acts on H^1(Z/n,π) through G^ρ. A class becomes trivial over E_ρ iff it lies in the orbit of the base point.
ideas.modern_name: Exact sequence of pointed sets in nonabelian cohomology; action of H^0 of the quotient on H^1 of the subgroup

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine working-out of standard nonabelian cohomology (twisted conjugacy, the orbit criterion) in the service of classifying torsion lifts. The only interest is as a step in the larger 'équation des lacets' manuscript.
transcription_corrections: 'scindages de (?)' — the reference is to the restricted extension of Z/nZ by π (π̃ → Z/nZ) from the previous page. The number in the image is hard to read; possibly (20) or (21).
'il est dans π ssi ... [-?-]' — the struck word after 'ssi' appears to be an abandoned start (perhaps 'i.e.'). The intended statement is 'il est dans π ssi [ᾱ,ρ]=1'.
The symbol written E in 'Soit α ∈ E' is the script ℰ used throughout, as on the next page.
